items.front: In Amazon RDS, the backup retention period of automated backups can be set {{c1::between 0 and 35 days}}.
items.extra: [Setting the backup retention period to 0 disables automated backups](../facts/rds.md#rds-backup-retention-range).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, the latest restorable time of a point-in-time restore is typically within the {{c1::last five minutes}}.
items.extra: You can restore to [any second during your retention period](../facts/rds.md#rds-faq-pitr-any-second-latest-restorable), up to that time.

items.front: In Amazon RDS, the failover of a Multi-AZ DB instance typically takes {{c1::60–120 seconds}}.
In Amazon RDS, the failover of a Multi-AZ DB cluster typically takes {{c1::under 35 seconds}}.
In Amazon RDS for MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL, one DB instance can have {{c1::up to 15 read replicas}}.
items.extra: AWS raised this limit on [October 20, 2022](../facts/rds.md#rds-change-read-replicas-15-2022-10).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, a DB instance can stay stopped for {{c1::7 consecutive days}}; then RDS starts it again.
In Amazon RDS Proxy, the failover time of Multi-AZ DB instances drops by {{c1::up to 66%}}.
In Amazon RDS, can a Multi-AZ DB cluster run RDS for SQL Server?
items.back: No. It runs RDS for MySQL or RDS for PostgreSQL.
items.extra: Multi-AZ DB clusters [aren't available with the following engines](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-cluster-engines-mysql-postgresql): Db2, MariaDB, Oracle and SQL Server.

items.front: In Amazon RDS, can the standby of a Multi-AZ DB instance serve read queries?
items.back: No. Use a read replica or a Multi-AZ DB cluster.
items.extra: [You can't use a standby replica](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-instance-not-read-scaling) to serve read traffic.

items.front: In Amazon RDS, can you turn on encryption for an existing unencrypted DB instance?
items.back: No. Restore from an encrypted copy of a snapshot.
items.extra: You can [only encrypt an Amazon RDS DB instance](../facts/rds.md#rds-encryption-only-at-create) when you create it. You can [encrypt a copy of an unencrypted snapshot](../facts/rds.md#rds-encryption-only-at-create) and restore from that copy.

items.front: In Amazon RDS, a database must survive an Availability Zone failure with automatic failover. What do you turn on?
items.back: A Multi-AZ deployment.
items.extra: It helps protect against [DB instance failure and Availability Zone disruption](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-instance-protects-az-disruption).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, reporting queries slow down the production database. What do you add?
items.back: A read replica for the reports.
items.extra: [Business reporting or data warehousing scenarios](../facts/rds.md#rds-read-replica-use-reporting) can run on a read replica instead of the production DB instance.

items.front: In Amazon RDS, many Lambda functions cause too many connections errors. What do you add?
items.back: RDS Proxy.
items.extra: A DB instance with ["too many connections" errors](../facts/rds-proxy.md#rds-proxy-candidate-too-many-connections) is a good candidate. The proxy keeps a [smaller number of long-lived connections](../facts/rds-proxy.md#rds-proxy-candidate-too-many-connections) to the database.

items.front: In Amazon RDS, does a point-in-time restore change the existing DB instance?
items.back: No. It creates a new DB instance with a new endpoint.
items.extra: The restore works by [creating a new DB instance](../facts/rds.md#rds-pitr-new-instance-within-retention), which is [created with a new endpoint](../facts/rds.md#rds-faq-restore-creates-new-instance).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, Multi-AZ or read replica: which one replicates synchronously?
items.back: Multi-AZ.
items.extra: Multi-AZ deployments use [synchronous replication](../facts/rds.md#rds-compare-replication-sync-async). Read replicas use [asynchronous replication](../facts/rds.md#rds-compare-replication-sync-async).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, can storage autoscaling reduce the allocated storage?
items.back: No. Storage autoscaling only grows the storage.
items.extra: [Autoscaling can't decrease the allocated storage](../facts/rds.md#rds-storage-autoscaling-cannot-decrease).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, storage use grows in ways nobody can predict. What do you turn on?
items.back: Storage autoscaling with a maximum storage threshold.
items.extra: [If your workload is unpredictable](../facts/rds.md#rds-storage-autoscaling-unpredictable), [it automatically scales up your storage](../facts/rds.md#rds-storage-autoscaling-unpredictable) when free space runs low.

items.front: In Amazon RDS, does Multi-AZ remove the downtime of an engine version upgrade?
items.back: No. The primary and the standby upgrade together.
items.extra: The upgrade [modifies both primary and secondary DB instances](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-engine-upgrade-both-down) and [causes downtime until the upgrade is complete](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-engine-upgrade-both-down).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, a major engine upgrade must be tested on a synced copy and switched with short downtime. What do you use?
items.back: A Blue/Green Deployment.
items.extra: Blue/Green Deployments fit [major or minor version database engine upgrades](../facts/rds.md#rds-faq-blue-green-use-cases) with [short, predictable downtime](../facts/rds.md#rds-faq-blue-green-use-cases).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, does a Multi-AZ failover keep the application's open connections?
items.back: No. The application reconnects to the same endpoint.
items.extra: RDS [changes the Domain Name System (DNS) record](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-failover-dns-change-reconnect), so you [re-establish any existing connections](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-failover-dns-change-reconnect).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, does Multi-AZ fail over because of a deadlock or a long-running query?
items.back: No. Those database operations cause no automatic failover.
items.extra: Multi-AZ deployments [do not failover automatically](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-no-failover-db-operations) for [long running queries, deadlocks, or database corruption errors](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-no-failover-db-operations).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, Multi-AZ DB instance or Multi-AZ DB cluster: which one has standbys that serve reads?
items.back: The Multi-AZ DB cluster.
items.extra: The two standbys of a cluster [can also serve read traffic](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-one-vs-two-standbys). The one standby of a Multi-AZ DB instance [doesn't serve read traffic](../facts/rds.md#rds-multi-az-one-vs-two-standbys).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, can you create a read replica when the source's backup retention period is 0?
items.back: No. Turn on automated backups first.
items.extra: You [enable automatic backups on the source DB instance](../facts/rds.md#rds-read-replica-requires-automated-backups) with a retention period of [a value other than 0](../facts/rds.md#rds-read-replica-requires-automated-backups).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, does a read replica take over automatically when the primary fails?
items.back: No. You promote it manually.
items.extra: Multi-AZ gives [automatic failover to standby](../facts/rds.md#rds-compare-failover-vs-promote). A read replica [can be manually promoted](../facts/rds.md#rds-compare-failover-vs-promote).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, the database must survive the loss of its whole Region. What do you create?
items.back: A cross-Region read replica.
items.extra: A read replica in another Region helps you [improve your disaster recovery capabilities.](../facts/rds.md#rds-cross-region-replica-use-cases)

items.front: In Amazon RDS, MySQL read replica or PostgreSQL read replica: which one can be made writable?
items.back: The RDS for MySQL read replica.
items.extra: You can enable a MySQL [read replica to be writable](../facts/rds.md#rds-replica-mysql-logical-writable). RDS for PostgreSQL does not allow a read replica [to be made writable](../facts/rds.md#rds-replica-postgresql-not-writable).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, a copy of today's database must be kept for many years. What do you take?
items.back: A manual DB snapshot.
items.extra: Manual snapshots [aren't subject to the backup retention period](../facts/rds.md#rds-manual-snapshots-dont-expire). [Snapshots don't expire.](../facts/rds.md#rds-manual-snapshots-dont-expire)

items.front: In Amazon RDS, do automated backups stay after you delete the DB instance?
items.back: No, unless you retain them. Take a final snapshot.
items.extra: Without Retain automated backups, [all automated backups are deleted](../facts/rds.md#rds-delete-instance-automated-backups-deleted). [Manual snapshots are not deleted](../facts/rds.md#rds-delete-instance-automated-backups-deleted).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, can you share an automated snapshot with another account directly?
items.back: No. Copy it to a manual snapshot first.
items.extra: You share it by [copying the automated snapshot](../facts/rds.md#rds-share-automated-copy-first) and then sharing the copy.

items.front: In Amazon RDS, can you share a snapshot that the AWS managed key encrypts?
items.back: No. Copy it with a customer managed key.
items.extra: A snapshot [encrypted using the default KMS key](../facts/rds.md#rds-share-default-kms-key-not-shareable) cannot be shared. Copy it [using the customer managed key](../facts/rds.md#rds-share-default-kms-key-not-shareable) and share the copy.

items.front: In Amazon RDS, does a stopped DB instance cost nothing?
items.back: No. Storage and backups are still billed.
items.extra: You are still [charged for provisioned storage (including Provisioned IOPS)](../facts/rds.md#rds-stop-billing), but [you're not charged for DB instance hours](../facts/rds.md#rds-stop-billing).

items.front: In Amazon RDS, a vendor agent must run on the host operating system of a Microsoft SQL Server database. What do you use?
items.back: Amazon RDS Custom.
items.extra: RDS Custom lets you [customize your database environment and operating system](../facts/rds.md#rds-custom-os-access). Standard Amazon RDS [doesn't let you access the underlying host](../facts/rds.md#rds-custom-os-access).
